reasons: Scale: the ring reads about 1.5-1.9x its listed size against the sage leaf. The ring's outer ellipse major axis is ~740 px, which is the true outer diameter of a US 7 ring, ~20.5 mm, so ~36 px/mm; the pave stones at ~37 px (~1.0 mm) agree. At that scale the leaf is only ~1022 px long including stem (stem end ~(800,1995) to tip ~(1347,1133)), ~28 mm projected. The blade is ~310 px wide (~9 mm). Blade width barely changes with camera angle, and the ring is ~2.1-2.4x that width. A ~55 mm sage leaf should be ~2.7x the ring's diameter and have a blade about as wide as the ring. The leaf is drawn almost face-on (outline not skewed, 2.1:1 blade aspect), so even allowing ~25% foreshortening the ring still reads >=1.4x. At phone size the ring looks as large as the leaf blade.
notes: The ring itself matches listing photo 0.jpg (same pose). Pave V with pointed apex (~12 visible stones per arm), plain polished middle V with soft apex, lower curved pave line (~20 visible stones), plain gold shank, yellow gold, clear round CZ. Construction and counts match.

Grade touched the product. On the a2g plate a specular highlight on the inner shank (~x540-597, y1412-1450) became a hard-edged mint-green patch, and a thin mint fringe runs along metal edges. The metal still reads gold at phone size, but the product should be masked out of the sage grade.
White-grey glare smudges on the glaze inside the ring at its base (~x600-780, y1500-1650) read as reflections, not as an extra piece.
A pale heart-shaped outline on the glaze loops around the ring base and leaf stem (~x430-1180, y1570-2110). This is a background artifact.
No text or logos. The frame reads sage, and the ring stands on the surface with plausible contact.
fix: Keep this ring render and angle, but make the sage leaf read ~55 mm. The leaf including stem should be ~2.7x the ring's outer diameter, with a blade roughly as wide as the ring (~0.8-1x ring diameter). Alternatively, shrink the ring ~40% relative to the current leaf. Mask the product before the sage grade so its highlights stay gold/neutral. Drop the glare smudge and the heart-shaped outline on the glaze.
